column1: # home-paths.tsv: the Home_Path_Class of each home-folder path (design.md,
# Data Models and "Session-time home writes"). Installed as
# and tools/fpdiff.py, and printed by "motanka install --dry-run".
# A glob is relative to the home folder. "*" and "?" match within one path
# component, "**" matches any number of them. The first line whose glob
# matches a path decides its class; a folder that no line matches takes
# the class of a path inside it ("<folder>/x"). Per-user setup skips a
# target that no line matches, and the motanka-core build fails on one
# ("user-setup --plan"). The session capture records a path no line
# What each class means for per-user setup (design.md, "Per-user setup")
# and for the session capture (paths a Motanka session creates without a
#   namespaced  only Motanka or vendored Upstream code uses the path:
#               written (ledgered, write-then-rename); not recorded by the
#               capture, because the Remover deletes the Namespaced_Paths
#   session     only the Motanka session reads it: ledgered, an existing
#               file backed up, then replaced by write-then-rename; a new
#               one the session creates is adopted (the Remover deletes it
#   app         an application file the user's other sessions may also
#               use: as session, but an existing file is left alone; a new
#   shared      read outside the Motanka session (Shared_File): never
#               written; shell integration may add one marked block to an
#               rc file when the user accepts it (6.5, 6.6); one the
#               session creates or changes is recorded as unplanned
#   desktop     written by Ubuntu's own session components (gnome-keyring,
#               xdg-user-dirs, PipeWire, the display manager, ...) at any
#               graphical login, the Motanka session's too: never written
#               by Motanka, left alone by the Remover, listed by "motanka
#               doctor" and left out of the Fingerprint comparison (the
# The capture never adopts a path that existed when the session started,
# and adds no line for a path that is in the User_Ledger already.
# Reviewed against Upstream's config/ tree at the stable pin (v4.5.0); each
# config/<x> is copied to ~/.config/<x>. Upstream files per entry:
#   git/config                                   shared: git reads it everywhere
# Other writes of per-user setup: the Hyprland fragment
# Writes during the Motanka session, found by the 26.04 round trip (first
# login, theme switch, menu install, web app) and classified here:
#   agent skill links that omarchy-provision-user makes (the override
#     writes them through the User_Ledger) in ~/.agents/skills,
#     ~/.hermes/skills and ~/.pi/agent/skills, and the theme files the
#     theme switch writes next to them (~/.claude/themes/omarchy.json,
#     and -ytdlp, run by install/user/chromium.sh, which per-user setup
#     skips, and by migrations)               app: Upstream's own files; the
#     activation file omarchy-input-method configure --defaults writes in
#     the first-run step; the folders are adopted when new and removed when
#                                                bus of every login reads it
# omarchy-provision-user also sets the XDG user folders, GTK bookmarks and

# --- Motanka's own file inside Upstream's namespace: listed before the
